speaker: charlie
text: Now for some science that'll blow your mind. Researchers at UCSF have discovered that DNA doesn't just store information - it literally folds like origami to create unique identities for every single cell in your body. Each fold is as unique as a snowflake, and these patterns act like barcodes that tell cells exactly what they should be doing.

speaker: alice
text: The really wild part is that neurons have to maintain these origami patterns for decades since they live as long as we do. Scientists think understanding this process could eventually help us rewire brain connections that have gone wrong in neurological disorders. Imagine being able to reprogram damaged brain circuits by teaching DNA new folding patterns.

speaker: charlie
text: It's like discovering your body has been using advanced 3D printing instructions this whole time, except the printer is microscopic and the blueprints fold themselves. The researcher behind this discovery switched from chemistry to neuroscience, which probably explains why he could see patterns others missed. Sometimes the best breakthroughs come from fresh eyes looking at old problems.
